solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cobblers restyled my jellies fawn, not navy (12, two words)

indicators.note: something restyled has been given a new form, so the letters are rearranged
'not' says the following item is to be taken out of the letters before rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: A cobbler has changed the colour of some sweets, avoiding dark blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' looks like shoemakers but is British slang for testicles (also nonsense), as is 'family jewels'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British slang terms for the testicles, so one stands in for the other.

clue.text: Start to booze after viral infection — a mistake

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
'after' places the next piece behind the earlier one in the answer

blocks.note: influenza is a viral infection
the first letter of booze

explanation.surface: After a bout of flu, taking the first drink proves an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A flub is an informal word for a blunder or botched attempt, so it can be called a mistake.

clue.text: No fan of poor recordings died amid distortion of 'hip' Louie A

indicators.note: distorting something twists it out of shape, so these letters are put in another order
'amid' places one piece in the middle of another

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the usual abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A hip character called Louie A hates bad recordings and suffers distorted sound.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside the rearranged letters, after AU.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiophile is a hi-fi enthusiast who cares about sound quality, so would never be a fan of poor recordings.

clue.text: Crowd accepting Our Lord brought up in menial occupation

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top, so backwards
a crowd accepting someone takes them inside itself

blocks.note: a mob is a crowd
JC stands for Jesus Christ

explanation.surface: A crowd welcomes Christ, raised in a humble trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A McJob is slang for a low-paid, low-status job, such as one in a fast-food chain: a menial occupation.

clue.text: Femme fatale lost old wreath

blocks.note: an obsolete past participle of lose
a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: A seductive woman has lost an old garland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' marks LORE as an archaic form, not a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the Rhine siren who lured boatmen to their deaths, the archetypal dangerous seductress.

clue.text: Stork joyful as baby is reaching us initially

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter of each of the words before it

blocks.clueFragment: joyful as baby is reaching us
blocks.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: The stork is happy as a baby is delivered to us.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the nursery tale that storks bring babies.
explanation.definitionFit: The jabiru is a large tropical American stork, so this species is a kind of stork.

clue.text: Organized ladies thrash old councillors

blocks.note: the Women's Institute, a British organization of women's groups
to tan someone's hide is to thrash them

explanation.surface: A group of organized women beat some elderly council members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organized' looks like an anagram signal but describes the ladies: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British network of local women's clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The witan was the Anglo-Saxon king's council of advisers, so its members were councillors of long ago.

clue.text: Forward, tireless worker following wing up (7, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means reading from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards
'following' places the worker after the other piece

blocks.note: a vane is the web of a feather, or a sail-like wing
the worker ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A tireless forward chasing up the wing in a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: En avant is French for forward or onward, used in English as a command to advance.

clue.text: Cutting tress badly he left for retreats

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters are jumbled
the pieces cutting into the jumbled word sit inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A clumsy barber cutting a lock of hair leaves for a quiet getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelters are places of refuge, and a retreat is likewise a safe or secluded place.

clue.text: Fish heads for lake, usually carrying eggs

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, which are the ones kept

blocks.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A fish swims to a lake, typically full of spawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Luce is an old name for the pike, especially a full-grown one, so it is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Nothing is omitted from pedestal for African chiefs

indicators.note: something omitted from a word is dropped out of it

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O
a basis is a base or foundation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nothing is left off the plinth prepared for some African leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: An oba is a hereditary chief or king in parts of West Africa, notably among the Yoruba.

clue.text: Sources of astringent bottled in a tube

indicators.note: 'bottled' is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An astringent remedy is sold packaged in a tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottled' reads as packaged but means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Butea is a genus of tropical trees whose gum, Bengal kino, is used as an astringent, so these plants are its source.

clue.text: Move slowly having entered church

blocks.note: someone who has entered is in
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone walks slowly up the aisle after coming into church.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to advance little by little, a slow, gradual movement.

clue.text: Where hacks write and yearn, as of old, for investment in share of lucky strike

definitions.text: investment in share of lucky strike

blocks.note: Grub Street, the old London home of hack writers
an archaic spelling of ache

explanation.surface: Poor writers dream of a stake in a gold rush find.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub Street was a London street of struggling hack writers, now a name for literary hackwork; ST is the usual abbreviation for street.
explanation.definitionFit: A grubstake is money or supplies advanced to a prospector in return for a share of whatever he finds.

clue.text: Family retreat housing special fair, offering helpful words?

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside

blocks.note: kin are one's family
a den is a private retreat
SP is an abbreviation for special
fair, as in middling, is OK

explanation.surface: A family's holiday home holds a fair where kind words are offered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kind-spoken speaks gently and kindly, so is offering helpful words; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Life story on a large scale? Nothing in it

indicators.note: 'in it' puts the nothing inside the phrase just given

blocks.note: something on a large scale is big
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An epic life story turns out to have nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A biog is an informal shortening of biography, the written story of someone's life.

clue.text: Minor gripe about Spanish town American has left

indicators.note: something that has left is no longer present, so it is dropped

blocks.note: c. is short for circa, about
Ávila is a walled town in central Spain
A is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A small complaint about a Spanish town that an American tourist has left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavil is a petty or trivial objection, so it is a minor complaint.

clue.text: Family jewels left in protection of friends down under

indicators.note: something in the protection of others is shielded within them

blocks.note: cobber is Australian slang for a mate
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Heirloom jewels are left in the safekeeping of Australian mates.
explanation.walkthrough: This answers 1-across in reverse: 'Family jewels' looks like heirlooms but means testicles, for which cobblers is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers (from rhyming slang cobblers' awls, balls) and family jewels are both slang for the testicles.

clue.text: Pet maybe swallowing pebble in Perth, for the knackers (one only)

definitions.note: knackers is the plural; the parenthesis asks for just one

indicators.note: an animal swallowing something takes it inside

blocks.note: a cat is one example of a pet
stane is the Scots word for stone; Perth is a Scottish city

explanation.surface: A pet swallows a stone in Perth and is sent off to the knacker's yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Knackers looks like the animal slaughterers (the knacker's yard), but is also a word for castanets or clappers.
explanation.definitionFit: Knackers are castanets or bones played as clappers, so a single one is a castanet.

clue.text: Even page in two-wheelers maybe frolics

indicators.note: 'in' puts the page inside the vehicles

blocks.note: a cart is one kind of two-wheeled vehicle
verso, the left-hand, even-numbered page of a book

explanation.surface: Even a page boy on bikes frolics around.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to leap or prance about playfully, which is to frolic.

clue.text: Boyfriend attending fancy do with men in high society (9, two words)

indicators.note: something fancy is elaborately made over, so these letters are rearranged
one person attending another goes alongside it, so the pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: a beau is a boyfriend
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boyfriend goes to a smart party among high-society men.
explanation.definitionFit: The beau monde, French for fine world, is the fashionable elite, i.e. high society.

clue.text: Child trapping limb in cooking pot

indicators.note: trapping something holds it inside

blocks.note: a mite is a small child
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A child gets an arm stuck in a cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite here is the French cooking pot, not the British yeast spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmite is a large covered earthenware or metal cooking pot used for stews and soups.

clue.text: I'll be received by Asian priest, alas, in his large tent?

indicators.note: being received by someone means being taken in by them

blocks.note: a shaman is a priest of Siberian and other Asian peoples
the I of I will; the contraction's 'll only supplies the verb of the surface
both are exclamations of regret

explanation.surface: A visitor will be welcomed by an Asian holy man, sadly, in his large tent.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside the priest before AH is added; 'his' points back to the priest, which the question mark acknowledges.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamianah is a large tent or awning used in India for gatherings, so it is a large tent.

clue.text: Opposition limiting Conservative tricks, extraordinary

indicators.note: limiting something hems it in on both sides

blocks.note: antis are people opposed to something
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: The opposition party is curbing the Conservatives' extraordinary tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Antics are grotesque or extravagant capers, extraordinary tricks; the old adjective antic means odd or bizarre.

clue.text: Number one and number two dead in the trenches?

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for number
a means one
childish slang for faeces

explanation.surface: A first and a second soldier lie dead in the trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one and number two' look like a pair of soldiers but split into three pieces, with number two the nursery euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoo, from French il n'y en a plus, was First World War soldiers' slang for finished, done for or killed.

clue.text: What promoters do is making mockery of fight's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: boos are jeers of derision
the last letter of fight

explanation.surface: Boxing promoters make a mockery of how a fight ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Promoters publicize and push something forward, which is to boost it.

clue.text: Runs laps limpingly — they'll reduce one to a standstill

definitions.text: they'll reduce one to a standstill

indicators.note: a runner moving limpingly is out of order, so the letters go out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An injured runner limps round the track, slowing almost to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarl-ups are traffic jams or muddles, which bring anyone caught in them to a standstill.

clue.text: Form of rust partly coloured orange

indicators.note: 'partly' says only part of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: letters inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A kind of rust that is part orange in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is a stage of rust fungi on plants, producing orange spores, so it is a form of the plant disease rust.

clue.text: One John Faraday, distinctly snooty

blocks.note: a means one
john is American slang for a toilet, as is loo
F is the symbol for the faraday, a unit of electric charge

explanation.surface: A man called John Faraday is plainly stuck-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John Faraday' reads as one person's name; both words are pieces, a toilet and a unit symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means cool and distant in manner, which comes across as markedly haughty or snooty.

clue.text: Puzzler: odd word in Shakespeare (meaning plausible?) — all thrown

indicators.note: something thrown out is discarded, so those letters go

blocks.note: probal, used by Iago in Othello, means probable or plausible
the letters of all with one L, as only these two appear at the end

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter is baffled by a strange Shakespearean word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all thrown' asks for the letters A and L to be removed from the Shakespearean word.
explanation.definitionFit: Prob is a common abbreviation of problem, and a problem is a puzzler.

clue.text: Pound fine, by the sound of it, in Scottish bank

indicators.note: this phrase says the word is to be heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: to bray is to pound or grind something fine, as in a mortar

explanation.surface: A one-pound fine charged in a Scottish bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound fine' looks like money, but is a verb: to grind small.
explanation.definitionFit: A brae is a Scots word for a hillside or the sloping bank of a river.

clue.text: Savoury dish served in liner badly done — it's greasy and orangey (9, two words)

a dish served in a place sits inside it

blocks.note: an olio is a spicy stew or hotchpotch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A savoury dish served on a cruise liner was badly cooked, greasy and orange-flavoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Neroli oil is an essential oil distilled from orange blossom, so it is both oily and orangey.

clue.text: Without starter cooks something for lunch?

indicators.note: without its starter a word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: to heat food is to cook it

explanation.surface: A cook prepares lunch with no first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like the first course of a meal but is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, so it is something you might have for lunch; the question mark marks a loose definition.

clue.text: Angus from Swiss Cottage?

indicators.note: 'from' says the answer is taken out of the words that follow, a run of their letters

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Is a man named Angus really from Swiss Cottage?
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is a district of north London, an unlikely home for a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus is a typically Scottish first name (and a Scottish county), so an Angus is an example of a Scotsman.

clue.text: Part in Seraglio going round English music halls

indicators.note: something going round another surrounds it

blocks.note: an oda is a room in a harem
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English singer has a part in Mozart's Seraglio, touring the music halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Odea, plural of odeum, are buildings for musical performances, so halls for music.

clue.text: Try bucking estro with the same steroid

indicators.note: a bucking horse throws itself about, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: to test is to try
taken as written
as in one and the same

explanation.surface: Try fighting against oestrogen with a similar steroid.
explanation.walkthrough: Estro is a real word (enthusiasm) and resembles the start of oestrogen, which makes the anagram fodder easy to overlook.
